## Verdict

[#2136](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2136) is the winner architecturally, but I would request changes before merging it.

[#2135](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2135) is narrower and handles cold-start timing more safely, but it stops halfway through the user-facing problem.

| Area | #2135 | #2136 |
|---|---|---|
| Parallel discovery | Good | Good |
| Broken-agent state | Separate `external` registry | Integrated into agent registry |
| User-visible failures | Missing | Added to `entire agent list` |
| Normal `agent.Get` behavior | Still reports unknown | Returns the actual load failure |
| Registry blast radius | Small | Larger, but well tested |
| Cold-start timeout | Safe but excessive at 10s | Known-broken at 300ms |
| Documentation | Limited to discovery package | Updates the protocol and CLI behavior |
| Windows deduplication | Incomplete | Dedupe uses derived agent name |

## Why #2136 wins

The strongest reason is that it finishes the behavior described in #2134.

In #2135, `external.Get`, `ReadyAgents`, and `BrokenAgents` have no production consumers outside the discovery package. They are used only by implementation code and tests. A broken plugin is retained internally, but `entire agent list` and the normal agent-resolution paths still cannot explain the failure. That is storage for a future solution, not the complete solution.

#2136 connects the pieces:

- Broken plugins become first-class registry entries.
- `agent.Get` can return the original load failure.
- Existing listing and detection APIs continue to expose only usable agents.
- `entire agent list` discovers plugins and prints a broken-agent section.
- The protocol documentation describes the new behavior.
- Built-in collision protection remains intact.
- Windows `.exe` and `.com` candidates deduplicate by their derived agent name.

The broader registry change is justified here. Keeping failures in a separate package makes every future consumer know about two registries. #2136 gives the agent registry one authoritative answer for a name: usable, broken, or absent.

## Required fixes in #2136

1. Raise the 300ms timeout.

The PR itself measures cold executions at 320 to 394ms, and concurrent cold executions above one second. It then warms every test binary before discovery. That makes CI reliable by avoiding the production behavior users will actually encounter.

I would use roughly 2 seconds per binary. Probes are parallel, so this does not become `N × 2s`. I would also remove general-purpose warming from `WriteExternalAgentBinary`; tests should override the timeout where needed.

2. Fix named-discovery memoization.

After a named binary fails, `agent.Get(name)` returns its recorded error. `discoverAndRegisterNamed` treats any error as absence and executes the same binary again. That contradicts the documented "once per binary per process" guarantee. The existing [review finding](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2136#discussion_r3862466671) is correct.

3. Preserve recorded errors in explicit CLI operations.

`entire agent add`, `remove`, and some `--agent` paths replace every `agent.Get` error with "Unknown agent." A broken installed plugin therefore still looks like a typo outside `agent list`. The [Bugbot finding](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2136#discussion_r3862488456) is valid.

Unknown-name errors and known-but-broken errors need different handling.

4. Fix invalid earlier PATH matches shadowing valid later binaries.

Both implementations mark a derived name as seen before confirming that the candidate is executable. A directory or non-executable file in an earlier PATH directory can therefore hide a valid binary later in PATH. This was reported against [#2135](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2135#discussion_r3862428971), but #2136 has the same ordering.

## What #2135 does better

Its 10-second timeout avoids false failures for freshly installed binaries. That value is too generous for interactive commands, but it is safer than knowingly shipping 300ms.

It also has a much smaller change footprint. If the requested scope were strictly "parallelize discovery and retain diagnostic state for later," #2135 would be easier to merge. But #2134 explicitly calls out explaining why installed plugins are unavailable, and #2135 does not deliver that to users.

Both PRs pass lint, unit, integration, Windows, and Vogon canary CI. The failed checks are review gates. #2135 also has an unresolved high-severity Entire finding, while #2136’s Entire gate only lacks approval.

My recommendation: continue with #2136, incorporate the four fixes above, and close #2135.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/pr2136-body.md
+<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
+https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1150
+<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->
+
+Stacked on #2134, which contains the two implementation plans. This PR implements the `claude-version.md` design and incorporates the follow-up review fixes.
+
+## Summary
+
+External agent discovery now collects candidates without executing them, probes each binary concurrently under its own budget, and applies results in stable PATH order. A slow or broken plugin no longer blocks later plugins, and load failures remain visible instead of disappearing into debug logs.
+
+## What changed
+
+- Store usable and broken external agents in the central agent registry. Registry walks still expose only usable agents, while `agent.Get` can return a recorded load failure.
+- Show broken plugins and their reasons in `entire agent list`.
+- Make `agent add`, `agent remove`, and explicit setup paths preserve load diagnostics instead of calling a known broken plugin "unknown".
+- Probe a failed named binary at most once per process. A different binary path with the same name may still be tried.
+- Let an invalid earlier PATH match, such as a directory or non-executable file, fall through to a runnable binary later on PATH. If no runnable binary exists, retain the first static failure for diagnostics.
+- Keep built-ins protected from PATH shadowing without executing the colliding binary.
+- Use a 10-second per-binary `info` budget. Probes run concurrently, so the aggregate bound remains roughly one budget. The earlier 300ms and 2s values failed on cold binaries, and healthy fixtures exceeded 5s under the full race suite.
+- Remove fixture warm-ups. Tests now execute fresh binaries through the same cold-start path users get.
+- Add typed unknown-agent classification so callers can distinguish absent names from installed but unloadable plugins.
+
+## Verification
